title: OmniVia Core Application Contract v1 - L0 evidence foundations
description: Provider-neutral wire shapes for the L0 evidence artifact and the `evidence.search` operation payload (ADR-039). `evidence.search` returns complete, append-preserving L0 evidence with exact provenance; an `EvidenceArtifact` is never a substitute for, and carries no reference implying it is, an accepted `GovernedRecord` -- it reuses only the generic `records.schema.json` provenance/temporal/source primitives that carry no governance-layer or governance-state assertion of their own. This document declares no root type; it is a definition container only.

EvidenceId.title: EvidenceId
EvidenceId.description: Stable identifier of one L0 evidence artifact, constant across its append-only provenance history. Distinct from `RecordId`: an evidence artifact is never itself a governed record.

EvidenceQuery.title: EvidenceQuery
EvidenceQuery.description: A caller-supplied, normalized search query for `evidence.search`. Normalization (case-folding, whitespace, tokenization) is caller-side; this document defines no normalization algorithm.

EvidenceChecksum.title: EvidenceChecksum
EvidenceChecksum.description: A content checksum, spelled `algorithm:hex-digest` (such as `sha256:9f86d0...`) so the digest is never ambiguous about which algorithm produced it. Provider-neutral: this contract does not mandate a specific algorithm.

MediaType.title: MediaType
MediaType.description: An IANA-style `type/subtype` media type string, such as `text/plain` or `application/json`.

EvidenceArtifact.title: EvidenceArtifact
EvidenceArtifact.description: One complete, append-preserving L0 evidence artifact: stable identity, workspace, exact source/native locator, applicable temporal instants, content checksum and media type, opaque metadata, permission/sensitivity labels, tombstone status, parser/ingestion status, and append-only provenance history. Carries no `GovernanceLayer`, `GovernanceState`, `RecordCurrentness`, or `authority_level` field: an evidence artifact is raw L0 material, never governed knowledge, and this shape must never be mistaken for a `GovernedRecord`.

evidence_id.description: Stable identifier of this evidence artifact.

workspace_id.description: Workspace this evidence artifact belongs to.

source.description: Exact source, native identifier, and locator this evidence was captured from.

temporal.description: The distinct instants applicable to this evidence: when observed, when ingested, and when this artifact was recorded, without collapsing them into one. `valid_from`/`valid_until`/`superseded_at` are rarely applicable to append-only L0 evidence and are typically absent.

content_checksum.description: Checksum of this evidence artifact's content, proving the content has not been altered since capture.

media_type.description: Media type of this evidence artifact's content.

metadata.description: Opaque metadata captured alongside this evidence artifact.

permission_labels.description: Open codes naming the access/permission labels attached to this evidence artifact, such as `restricted` or `team_only`. May be empty when no label applies.

sensitivity.description: Open code naming this evidence artifact's sensitivity classification, such as `public` or `confidential`.

tombstoned.description: True when this evidence artifact has been tombstoned. A tombstoned artifact's append-only provenance history is never erased; tombstoning is itself recorded as a provenance entry.

parser_status.description: Open code naming the status of parsing this evidence artifact's content, such as `parsed` or `parse_failed`.

ingestion_status.description: Open code naming the status of ingesting this evidence artifact, such as `ingested` or `quarantined`.

provenance_history.description: Append-only history of actions taken on this evidence artifact. Never truncated or rewritten; a correction is a new entry, not an edit to a prior one. Never empty: even the first capture of this artifact is itself a provenance entry, so an artifact with no recorded history entry would be an unaudited state.

import_run_id.description: Names the import job/run that produced this evidence artifact, when it was produced by one. Typed as `OpaqueToken` because it is drawn from exactly the same opaque token domain as `JobIdentity.job_id` and `ImportCompletionResult.import_run_id`: the completion contract promises this backlink names the run that created this evidence, and spelled in any narrower vocabulary it could not hold every job id the contract admits -- a run such as `job/opaque-token` could complete and then have no writable backlink at all.

EvidenceSearchInput.title: EvidenceSearchInput
EvidenceSearchInput.description: Input for `evidence.search`. Workspace-scoped: the workspace is the request envelope's selected workspace; this payload never carries a second, independent workspace identifier.

sensitivity.description: Restrict results to this sensitivity classification, when set.

include_tombstoned.description: Whether tombstoned evidence artifacts may be included. Absent means the server's default (excluded).

limit.description: Bounded maximum number of evidence artifacts to return in this page.

page.description: Continuation position from a prior page, when paging.

EvidenceSearchResult.title: EvidenceSearchResult
EvidenceSearchResult.description: Result of `evidence.search`: complete, append-preserving L0 evidence artifacts with exact provenance. Never substitutes a `GovernedRecord` for an evidence artifact.

page.description: Continuation position for the next page, absent on the last page.

EvidenceCaptureInput.title: EvidenceCaptureInput
EvidenceCaptureInput.description: Input for `evidence.capture`: one caller-supplied UTF-8 text or Markdown artifact to record synchronously as immutable L0 evidence in the selected workspace, for small direct submissions such as notes, excerpts, and model-visible source material. Workspace-scoped: the workspace is the request envelope's selected workspace; this payload never carries a second, independent workspace identifier, nor any path, URL, credential, principal, grant, parser, layer, governance, or storage option. Carries exactly one of `text`/`content_base64`; enforcing that exclusivity, the strict base64/UTF-8 decode, and the decoded-byte bound is a semantic-validation concern, not a wire-shape one.

source_native_id.description: Caller-chosen opaque identifier of this submission within the existing source-identity domain.

media_type.description: Media type of the submitted content. Restricted to `text/plain` or `text/markdown`; parameters such as `charset=` are forbidden -- enforcing that allowlist is a semantic-validation concern, not a wire-shape one.

text.description: UTF-8 text form of the content. Exactly one of `text`/`content_base64` is required.

content_base64.description: Strict RFC 4648 base64 of UTF-8 bytes. Exactly one of `text`/`content_base64` is required.

source_version.description: Optional provenance claim in the existing identifier domain. Does not permit overwrite or create a second identity version.

event_at.description: Optional canonical event-time claim. When `observed_at` is also present, `event_at` must not be later -- a semantic-validation concern, not a wire-shape one.

EvidenceCaptureResult.title: EvidenceCaptureResult
EvidenceCaptureResult.description: Result of `evidence.capture`: the stored evidence artifact's identity and stable source. `capture_disposition` is `created` for the first committed capture and `already_captured` for a same-source, identical-claims capture resolved under the existing collision rules; a replay of the original idempotency key returns this stored canonical result and never rewrites it.

evidence_id.description: Stable identifier of the stored evidence artifact.

source.description: The persisted source reference. `kind` is always `direct_submission` for this operation -- enforcing that is a semantic-validation concern, not a wire-shape one.

media_type.description: Media type of the stored content.

content_checksum.description: Checksum of the decoded content, computed over the decoded bytes before persistence. The digest is always lowercase hexadecimal -- enforcing that is a semantic-validation concern, not a wire-shape one.

content_length_bytes.description: Length of the decoded content in bytes.

capture_disposition.description: Whether this call created a new evidence artifact (`created`) or resolved to an existing one under the collision rules (`already_captured`) -- enforcing that closed vocabulary is a semantic-validation concern, not a wire-shape one.

DocumentCaptureBase.title: DocumentCaptureBase
DocumentCaptureBase.description: Closed capture-head precondition. `creation` carries no capture id; `existing` carries the observed successful capture id when one existed and omits it when the observed head was explicitly empty.

capture_id.description: Observed successful capture for an existing document, absent when explicitly empty.

DocumentOriginalBindingInput.title: DocumentOriginalBindingInput
DocumentOriginalBindingInput.description: Opaque native-owner lineage for the snapshot; it contains no path or bookmark bytes.

root_ref.description: Opaque selected-root reference for a root member.

member_ref.description: Opaque frozen member reference under the selected root.

DocumentProcessingProfileInput.title: DocumentProcessingProfileInput
DocumentProcessingProfileInput.description: Exact immutable processing profile selection frozen by the native caller.

DocumentReprocessProfileSelection.title: DocumentReprocessProfileSelection
DocumentReprocessProfileSelection.description: One approved processing-profile selection a caller takes verbatim from `document.history` and sends back in `document.reprocess`. It is a separate type from `DocumentProcessingProfileInput` because it carries a third field that only a reprocess can have: the exact immutable profile the selection was reported to resolve to. A capture has no such digest to name -- its profile is resolved after admission -- so that input keeps its two fields. `expected_profile_digest` is a precondition, not a preference: Core recomputes the profile from the named reference, revision, the capture's media type and the installation's resources, and refuses the request before any execution when the recomputed identity differs, so a newer profile or newer resources are never substituted beneath a request that named this one.

profile_ref.description: Immutable processing-profile reference, exactly as `document.history` reported it approved for this capture.

revision.description: Exact approved profile revision reported with that reference.

expected_profile_digest.description: The immutable profile identity Core reported this selection resolves to. Core refuses rather than executing a different one.

DocumentConsentInput.title: DocumentConsentInput
DocumentConsentInput.description: Standing-consent lineage required for automatic capture.

dirty_epoch.description: Native change epoch that authorised this snapshot.

member_id.description: Frozen member in the reviewed manifest.

DocumentCaptureInput.title: DocumentCaptureInput
DocumentCaptureInput.description: Closed input for `document.capture`. Carries exactly one bounded inline snapshot or an immutable server-issued staged-source descriptor plus opaque lineage; no original path, bookmark, credential, parser name, arbitrary endpoint, principal, or workspace override is accepted. Exact-one content selection is enforced semantically.

document_id.description: Logical document identity selected before transfer.

content_base64.description: Strict RFC 4648 base64 of a small complete immutable snapshot, bounded so the whole request remains inside OVC1.

staged_source.description: Server-issued immutable descriptor for a snapshot transferred over the bounded local binary staging protocol.

media_type.description: Validated media type of the snapshot.

requested_source_identity.description: Stable caller-selected source identity for this capture intent.

target_binding_revision.description: Trusted destination binding revision frozen before publication.

processing_profile.description: Exact processing profile requested for the admitted capture.

bulk_origin.description: Frozen folder-run lineage for bulk work.

DocumentCaptureResult.title: DocumentCaptureResult
DocumentCaptureResult.description: Canonical receipt for one document capture admission or exact replay.

document_id.description: Logical document associated with the capture.

source_digest.description: Core-computed SHA-256 identity of admitted bytes.

became_head.description: Whether this capture became the current successful capture.

DocumentExtractionBase.title: DocumentExtractionBase
DocumentExtractionBase.description: Closed successful-extraction-head precondition for reprocessing. The object is always required; `extraction_id` is present when the caller observed a successful extraction head and absent when it explicitly observed no successful extraction.

extraction_id.description: Observed successful extraction revision, absent only for an explicitly empty extraction head.

DocumentReprocessInput.title: DocumentReprocessInput
DocumentReprocessInput.description: Closed input for `document.reprocess`. Selects one already-retained immutable capture, one exact approved processing-profile revision together with the immutable profile identity that revision was reported to resolve to, and the observed successful extraction head. It accepts no source bytes, original path, URL, bookmark, parser implementation, arbitrary profile JSON, principal or workspace override.

capture_id.description: Retained immutable capture to process again without rereading its original.

processing_profile.description: Exact approved processing profile selected for the new extraction revision, with the profile identity it must resolve to.

DocumentReprocessResult.title: DocumentReprocessResult
DocumentReprocessResult.description: Canonical terminal receipt for one retained-copy reprocess or exact replay.

document_id.description: Logical document associated with the retained capture.

capture_id.description: Exact retained capture that was reprocessed.

profile_digest.description: Core-computed identity of the immutable processing profile.

publication_disposition.description: Whether this revision atomically replaced retrieval, remained historical, was superseded or was fenced.

became_head.description: Whether this extraction became the document's successful retrieval head.

output_digest.description: Digest of the qualified extraction output when the terminal state produced one.

DocumentHistoryInput.title: DocumentHistoryInput
DocumentHistoryInput.description: Closed input for `document.history`. Selects exactly one logical document owned by the request envelope's selected workspace; it carries no second workspace identifier and no path, bookmark, credential, principal, parser name or workspace override, and no selector that could widen the read past that one document. Pagination is deterministic: `limit` bounds each of the two returned histories separately, and `page` resumes an earlier read at the exact position it reached.

document_id.description: Logical document whose canonical intake history is read.

limit.description: Bounded maximum number of source captures, and of extraction revisions, to return in this page. Absent means the server's default.

page.description: Continuation position from a prior page, when paging.

DocumentHistoryAction.title: DocumentHistoryAction
DocumentHistoryAction.description: One action Core states the availability of, with the exact reason when it is unavailable. A caller offers a control only for an action reported `available`, and otherwise shows the stated reason rather than a control that cannot work. v1 reports `reprocess_captured_copy` against one retained capture and `refresh_original` against the document. An action code this build does not recognise is preserved and not offered.

action.description: Open code naming the action, such as `reprocess_captured_copy` or `refresh_original`.

available.description: Whether Core will accept this action now.

unavailable_reason.description: Open code naming why the action is unavailable, present exactly when `available` is false -- enforcing that is a semantic-validation concern, not a wire-shape one.

DocumentReprocessProfileOption.title: DocumentReprocessProfileOption
DocumentReprocessProfileOption.description: One processing-profile selection Core reports as approved and available for reprocessing this exact retained capture, and will accept in a `document.reprocess` request naming that capture. `profile_digest` is the immutable profile the selection resolves to for this capture's media type now, so a caller can prove the revision it was offered is the revision that ran, and a newer profile or newer resources are never substituted beneath a request that named this one. A caller never synthesises a reference or revision of its own.

profile_ref.description: Immutable processing-profile reference to send in `document.reprocess`.

revision.description: Exact approved profile revision to send with that reference.

processing_mode.description: Closed value `text_only` or `text_and_local_ocr`, as this capture's media type resolves the selection.

profile_digest.description: Core-computed identity of the immutable profile this selection resolves to for this capture.

DocumentExtractionProfileSummary.title: DocumentExtractionProfileSummary
DocumentExtractionProfileSummary.description: The immutable processing profile one extraction revision was produced under. `digest` is the profile's canonical identity and the only field a caller may compare for sameness. `decoder_build` is the exact decoder-build string the profile records, which carries the profile reference and revision the admitting request froze. The profile body itself -- its resource ceilings, pinned model hashes, parser feature list and unknown-feature rules -- is not exposed.

digest.description: Core-computed identity of the immutable profile.

decoder_build.description: The profile's exact recorded decoder build, including the frozen profile reference and revision.

embedded_image_ocr.description: Whether this profile examined qualified embedded raster images for text.

ocr_languages.description: The ordered recognition languages this profile selected, at most three. Empty when the profile ran no local OCR. Three is the normative maximum a selection may hold, so a summary naming a fourth describes a selection Core would itself have refused.

DocumentCaptureHistoryEntry.title: DocumentCaptureHistoryEntry
DocumentCaptureHistoryEntry.description: One immutable source capture of this document, exactly as Core admitted it. `is_current_source` is read from the document's own source head and is never inferred from `capture_sequence`, from arrival order or from any timestamp. Retention is this capture's own disposition and moves independently of the document's source state. A capture that is not the current source keeps its full attribution rather than losing it. No source bytes, original filesystem path, bookmark material, credential or caller-supplied display claim appears here.

capture_id.description: Canonical immutable capture identifier, exactly as `document.reprocess` accepts it.

capture_sequence.description: This capture's admission sequence within the document. An ordering fact, never a currentness claim.

evidence_id.description: Retained canonical evidence artifact holding the captured bytes.

source_digest.description: Core-computed identity of the admitted bytes.

media_type.description: Validated media type of the captured snapshot.

requested_source_identity.description: Stable caller-selected source identity this capture was admitted under.

capture_disposition.description: Closed value `head_eligible` or `historical_only`, as admission decided it.

disposition_reason.description: Closed reason the disposition was assigned: `eligible`, `removed_source`, `superseded_generation`, `disconnected_generation`, `creation_conflict` or `stale_base`.

is_current_source.description: Whether this exact capture is the document's current source head, read from the head itself.

retention_state.description: Closed value `retained`, `expired` or `deleted` for this capture's bytes.

capture_retention_generation.description: Core-owned generation of this capture's retained/eligible disposition.

source_removal_generation.description: The logical-source removal generation frozen at this capture's admission.

requested_profile.description: The processing profile this capture requested when it was admitted. Its extractions are reported separately and may name a different profile.

processing_state.description: Closed value `pending` while Core still owns an unsettled processing obligation for this capture, `settled` once that obligation has settled, or `not_queued` when none was recorded. Never a retrieval claim.

expected_base_capture_id.description: The successful capture head this capture froze as its base, absent when it observed none.

retention_changed_at.description: When this capture's retention state last changed, absent when Core records no retention row.

actions.description: The actions Core states the availability of for this exact capture.

reprocess_profiles.description: The approved profile selections Core will accept for reprocessing this capture. Empty when reprocessing is unavailable, in which case `actions` carries the reason.

DocumentExtractionHistoryEntry.title: DocumentExtractionHistoryEntry
DocumentExtractionHistoryEntry.description: One immutable extraction revision over one of this document's captures. `is_current_extraction` is read from the document's own extraction head and is never inferred from `document_ordinal`, from arrival order or from any timestamp. The extraction head is independent of the source head: a revision over an older capture can never make that capture the current source, and a revision that reaches a terminal state without being promoted is historical-only rather than a success. `result_state` and `publication_disposition` are absent while no terminal result exists, which is a pending extraction and not a failed one.

extraction_revision_id.description: Canonical immutable extraction revision identifier, exactly as `document.reprocess` expects as a base.

capture_id.description: The exact capture whose retained bytes this revision read.

document_ordinal.description: This revision's ordering position among all of the document's extractions. An ordering fact, never a currentness claim.

extraction_sequence.description: This revision's ordering position among the extractions of its own capture.

profile.description: The exact immutable profile this revision ran under.

expected_base_extraction_id.description: The successful extraction head this revision froze as its base, absent when it observed none.

head_eligible.description: Whether admission found this revision's frozen base still current, which is the only way it could ever be promoted.

is_current_extraction.description: Whether this exact revision is the document's current retrieval head, read from the head itself.

result_state.description: Closed terminal state `succeeded`, `partial`, `unsupported` or `failed`. Absent while the revision has no terminal result.

publication_disposition.description: Closed value `promoted`, `superseded`, `historical_only`, `fenced_removal`, `fenced_retention` or `not_published`. Absent while the revision has no terminal result.

output_digest.description: Digest of the qualified extraction output, present only when the terminal state produced one.

worker_build.description: The worker build that produced the terminal result, absent while there is none.

admitted_at.description: When Core admitted this extraction revision.

completed_at.description: When this revision reached its terminal result, absent while it has none.

DocumentSourceHeadState.title: DocumentSourceHeadState
DocumentSourceHeadState.description: The document's source side: its current successful capture when it has one, and the Core-owned generation that governs removal and suppression. Independent of the extraction head -- a new capture does not move the extraction head and a new extraction does not move this one. `original_binding_state` is a route fact only; it carries no opaque owner reference, no path and no bookmark material, and it is not a statement about whether any capture is retrievable.

source_state.description: Closed value `active` or `removed` for the logical source.

source_removal_generation.description: Core-owned generation that advances on removal, suppression change and authorised restoration.

current_capture_id.description: The document's current successful capture, absent when it explicitly has none.

capture_head_sequence.description: The sequence of the current successful capture, zero when there is none.

original_binding_state.description: Closed value `connected` when at least one original route for this document is connected, `disconnected` when routes exist but none is connected, or `none` when Core records no original route at all.

updated_at.description: When either head or the source state last changed.

DocumentExtractionHeadState.title: DocumentExtractionHeadState
DocumentExtractionHeadState.description: The document's extraction side: its current retrieval head when it has one, and whether retrieval rows are actually published for it. Independent of the source head. `retrieval_state` is `retrievable` only when Core currently publishes retrieval rows for this document; a pending, failed or historical-only extraction leaves whatever was already published in place rather than replacing it.

current_extraction_id.description: The document's current successful extraction, absent when it explicitly has none.

extraction_head_ordinal.description: The document ordinal of the current successful extraction, zero when there is none.

retrieval_state.description: Closed value `retrievable` when Core publishes retrieval rows for this document now, otherwise `none`.

published_at.description: When the published retrieval projection was written, absent when nothing is published.

DocumentHistoryResult.title: DocumentHistoryResult
DocumentHistoryResult.description: Result of `document.history`: the authoritative Core intake history of one logical document. Immutable source captures and extraction revisions are reported as two separate histories with two separate heads, because they move independently; neither list's order states which member is current, and the two head states are the only statements of currentness. `capture_count` and `extraction_count` are the complete totals, so a caller paging through the histories can say truthfully how much it has seen. Nothing here carries source bytes, an original filesystem path, bookmark material, a credential, a raw profile body or any locally held delivery receipt: local activity remains a separate, non-canonical record.

document_id.description: The logical document this history describes.

created_at.description: When Core created the logical document.

source.description: The independent source head and source state.

extraction.description: The independent extraction head and retrieval state.

captures.description: This page of the document's immutable source captures, in ascending `capture_sequence` order.

capture_count.description: Total number of source captures this document has, across every page.

extractions.description: This page of the document's immutable extraction revisions, in ascending `document_ordinal` order.

extraction_count.description: Total number of extraction revisions this document has, across every page.

actions.description: The document-level actions Core states the availability of.

page.description: Continuation position for the next page. A continuation token means at least one of the two histories has more to read; `{}` means both are exhausted.
